item.title: Amami Sea Turtle Nesting Season — Guide
item.description: The warm, clear seas and beaches of Amami Oshima and Kagoshima’s southern islands are important nesting grounds for sea turtles, and witnessing their life cycle is a moving wildlife experience. From around May to August, female sea turtles — including loggerhead and green turtles — return to the beaches where they were born to come ashore at night, dig nests in the sand and lay their eggs, before returning to the sea.

item.title: Wakayama's Marine Museums and Aquariums: Life of the Kuroshio — Guide
item.description: The Kii Peninsula’s coast is washed by the warm Kuroshio current, which carries subtropical marine life far north and makes Wakayama’s waters some of the richest in Japan — home to coral, sea turtles and an enormous variety of fish. The prefecture’s marine museums and aquariums showcase this abundance, with displays on the Kuroshio ecosystem, coral communities and the loggerhead sea turtles that nest on local beaches, alongside touch pools and conservation exhibits.

item.title: Wakayama Nature: Kumano Kodo Trails, Nachi Falls & Sea Turtle Beaches
item.description: The Kii Peninsula, which makes up most of Wakayama Prefecture, contains some of the most biologically and geologically diverse terrain in Japan. Warm, rain-drenched mountains rise abruptly from a Pacific coastline shaped by the Kuroshio Current — Japan’s equivalent of the Gulf Stream — moderating the climate just enough to support subtropical species more than 300 kilometres north of their usual range. The result is a landscape where ancient cedar forests meet coral reefs, where Japan’s tallest waterfall drops into UNESCO-listed primeval forest, and where sea turtles nest on beaches that also see summer holidaymakers from Osaka.
